To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed FOFPID controller with/without RFB shows superior performance in comparison with the other control schemes under different operating conditions.
the FOFPID controller is a promising candidate for AGC of reconfigured multi-area multi-source power systems in the presence of RFB.
the proposed FOFPID controller with RFB is an efficient and effective tool for AGC of reorganized multi-area multi-source power systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) AGC of reformed multi-area multi-source power systems; (2) application of fractional-order fuzzy PID; (3) application of BFOA; (4) incorporation of RFB; (5) incorporating GRC; and (6) demonstrating robustness.
AGC of reconfigured multi-area multi-source power systems incorporating RFB under deregulation.
the development and implementation of a new FOFPID controller to achieve fast and accurate AGC of the restructured multi-source power systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suggested approach is a promising one for the effective AGC of reorganized power systems in the presence/ absence of RFB.
the FOFPID controller with RFB is a suitable choice for AGC of reconfigured hydrothermal power systems in the presence of generation rate constraints.
the proposed FOFPID controller with RFB is an efficient and robust control scheme for the restructured multi-area hydrothermal systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FOFPID controller is an effective tool for AGC of re-structured multi-area multi source power systems with/without RFBs.
the proposed FOFPID controller is a better choice to be implemented in restructured multi-area systems for AGC.
FOFPID control strategy along with RFB can be used for efficient and robust AGC of reformed multi-area multi-source power systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed FOFPID controller with/without RFB is a promising control strategy to ensure reliable operation and economic efficiency of the restructured multi-area hydrothermal power systems in a competitive market.
the proposed FOFPID controller with RFB is capable of providing better AGC performance in terms of frequency and tie-line power deviations, and settling time as compared to the existing methods.
the suggested approach can be implemented in AGC of multi-area power systems to achieve superior performance.
